title: 04 · Compression Tiers & CoT Dynamics
desc: Space-time CoT trade-off across 116 experimental runs, mild-compression denoising acceleration (<1.0x CoT), full-lifecycle cost amortization formula, and BT-L0..BT-L3 operational tiers.
body: Chapter 04 — Standardized Compression Tiers & Chain-of-Thought Cognitive Dynamics ← Chapter 03: Core Axioms & Grammar · Back to Portal (README_EN) · Next: Chapter 05 — Agentic Protocol Stack & SMFT → 4.1 Does Compression Force Models to "Think Harder"? (The Space-Time Trade-Off) A critical systems question is whether feeding dense symbolic text into an LLM forces the reader model to spend extra Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning tokens mentally decompressing the text back into natural language—wiping out cheap input-token savings with expensive output-token generation. Synthesizing 116 experimental runs across 2,128 QuALITY questions and 2,586 MeetingBank questions ( arXiv:2606.19857 §4.3), BT-Spec v1.0 codifies three laws of reasoning overhead: flowchart TD subgraph Regimes["Three Cognitive Regimes Across Context Retention Ratios"] R1["Mild Compression (45%–65% Retention): Denoising Acceleration — CoT multiplier drops BELOW uncompressed baseline (< 1.0x)"] R2["Canonical Sweet Spot (25%–40% Retention): ~96%–99.5% semantic fidelity; CoT multiplier matches or beats Summary & LLMLingua-2"] R3["Extreme Over-Compression (< 10% Retention): Evidence sparsity triggers Space-Time Trade-Off — CoT tokens surge to bridge gaps"] end R1 --> R2 --> R3 Law I: Zero Intrinsic Surface Decoding Tax At matched retention ratios, BabelTele induces CoT multipliers comparable to or lower than human-readable summaries and LLMLingua-2. LLMs do not translate BabelTele into English prose inside CoT; they reason directly over the symbolic graph. Law II: Denoising Acceleration in Mild Compression Between 40% and 60% retention, BabelTele frequently achieves a CoT token multiplier < 1.0x relative to reading uncompressed text. Stripping conversational fluff and distracting tangents sharpens attention routing and shortens reasoning traces. Law III: The Extreme Sparsity Boundary When retention drops below 10% ( >90% compression), CoT tokens rise sharply across all compression methods as models expend reasoning steps reconstructing sparse evidence. 💡 Tip Full-Lifecycle Cost Amortization Law Real production ROI must account for compilation prefill/decode, $N$ -time downstream consumption, reader CoT overhead, and verification: $$\text{Cost}_{\text{total}} = \underbrace{C_{\text{comp\_in}}(x) + C_{\text{comp\_out}}(z)}_{\text{One-Time Compilation}} + N \cdot \Big[ \underbrace{C_{\text{read\_in}}(z)}_{\text{Compressed Read}} + \underbrace{C_{\text{CoT\_out}}(R, z)}_{\text{Reader CoT}} \Big] + C_{\text{audit}}$$ Negative ROI ( $N = 1$ short prompts) : Never invoke an LLM compressor on a single-use short prompt where compilation cost exceeds read savings. High ROI ( $N \ge 3$ or Window-Overflow) : Pre-compiling static RAG corpora, persistent multi-turn agent memory, multi-agent broadcast buses, and multi-million-token repository compression amortizes compilation cost rapidly. 4.2 Standardized Compression Tiers ( BT-L0 ~ BT-L3 ) Because raw LLM compressors vary wildly in default aggressiveness (e.g., Gemini 3.1 Pro exceeds 95% compression by default while GPT-5.4 averages ~75% ), BT-Spec v1.0 standardizes four operational tiers: Tier Identifier Target Retention (Token Savings) Structural Profile Primary Engineering Use Case Level 0 BT-L0 Telegraphic Prose 55% – 70% (Saves 30%–45%) Monolingual telegraphese: drops articles, filler, and politeness while keeping human skimmability. Human-monitored semi-automated operational logs. Level 1 BT-L1 Structured Hybrid 40% – 55% (Saves 45%–60%) Section headers #Sec , flat K=V bindings, causal arrows => ; triggers CoT denoising ( <1.0x ) . Short-session working memory (~700–2,000 token dialogue sessions; 96.48% LoCoMo retention). Level 2 BT-L2 Canonical BabelTele 25% – 40% (Saves 60%–75%) Recommended Default : Full omnilingual token minimization + six operator clusters + verbatim hard-data lock. A2A multi-agent messaging, pre-compiled RAG chunks, cross-model state transfer . Level 3 BT-L3 Extreme / ASCII Skeleton 5% – 25% (Saves 75%–95%) Ultra-dense single-char ASCII skeleton ( BT-L3-ASCII ); reserved for frontier compressor-reader pairs. Breaking physical context limits (e.g., fitting 1.65M-token code repos into 200K–256K windows). Next Chapter : Chapter 05 — The Agentic Protocol Stack & Semantic Merkle Memory Tree →

body: Chapter 05 — The Agentic Protocol Stack & Semantic Merkle Memory Tree ← Chapter 04: Compression Tiers & CoT Dynamics · Back to Portal (README_EN) · Next: Chapter 06 — Cross-Model Consensus & Audit Gateway → 5.1 The Five-Layer Agentic Communication Stack Popular commentary sometimes frames BabelTele as an adversarial replacement that will "wipe out" human-designed protocols like MCP and A2A. Architecturally, MCP and A2A govern connectivity and task routing, whereas BabelTele governs semantic payload density —mirroring how Protobuf or Brotli operates atop HTTP/2 and TCP/IP: flowchart TB L5["L5 Human Presentation Layer: Decoded to natural language strictly at human UX / approval boundaries"] L4["L4 Semantic Payload Layer (BabelTele): BT-L1/L2/L3 omnilingual symbolic graph encoding"] L3["L3 Agent Orchestration Layer (A2A): Agent Cards, task delegation & lifecycle state machines"] L2["L2 Tool & Context Bus Layer (MCP): Databases, local filesystems & external API bindings"] L1["L1 Transport & Framing Layer: HTTP/2 · SSE · WebSocket · JSON-RPC 2.0"] L5 <--> L4 <--> L3 <--> L2 <--> L1 Standard JSON-RPC Envelope Metadata ( content_encoding ) BabelTele integrates non-invasively into standard A2A and MCP JSON-RPC envelopes via metadata headers: Copy { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "tasks/send", "params": { "id": "task_9f82a1", "message": { "role": "agent", "metadata": { "content_encoding": "babeltele/1.0", "bt_tier": "BT-L2", "compressor_model": "claude-sonnet-4.6", "source_sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924..." }, "parts": [ { "type": "text", "text": "#RepoAudit @[Auth=src/auth/jwt.ts]: !vuln:alg=='none'@L142 & !exp_check => fix:?header.alg∉[RS256,EdDSA]=>reject(401)." } ] } } } Multi-Agent Empirical Gains (DeepResearch Bench) Homogeneous Multi-Agent (Gemini 3.1 Pro $\leftrightarrow$ Gemini 3.1 Pro) : 38.96% communication token reduction at 96.6% baseline score retention. Heterogeneous Multi-Agent (Gemini 3.1 Pro $\leftrightarrow$ GPT-5.4) : 44.21% communication token reduction at 99.7% baseline score retention. 5.2 Reclaiming Context Space: Semantic Merkle Folding Tree (SMFT) In §7 of the Bitcoin Whitepaper ( Reclaiming Disk Space ), Satoshi Nakamoto introduced Merkle Tree pruning so historical transactions could be hashed upward without exhausting node disk storage. Long-horizon LLM agents confront an identical bottleneck: unbounded dialogue and tool-output streams rapidly saturate context windows and degrade retrieval fidelity. Synthesizing arXiv:2606.19857 (LoCoMo memory evaluation) and open-source hierarchical folding ( compressed-context ), BT-Spec v1.0 defines the Semantic Merkle Folding Tree (SMFT) : flowchart TD subgraph Cold_Store["Persistent Cold Storage (Verbatim Transcripts + Hash Pointers)"] Raw1["Raw Turns #1–#20"] Raw2["Raw Turns #21–#40"] Raw3["Raw Turns #41–#60"] Raw4["Raw Turns #61–#80"] end subgraph Active_Window["Active LLM Context Window"] T1_A["[T1 Block #1] {h1}"] T1_B["[T1 Block #2] {h1}"] T2_AB["[T2 Merged Digest #1+#2] {h2} (BT-L2)"] T1_C["[T1 Retained Block #3] {h1} (BT-L1)"] T1_D["[T1 Retained Block #4] {h1} (BT-L1)"] Active["Active Raw Dialogue (#81–Present)"] end Raw1 --> T1_A Raw2 --> T1_B T1_A & T1_B --> T2_AB Raw3 --> T1_C Raw4 --> T1_D Active Frontier : Ongoing turns stay in raw natural language for zero-latency responsiveness. T1 Checkpoint Folding : Overflowing turns are compiled via BT-Memory ( BT-P1 ) into self-contained [T1] {h1} blocks while raw messages move to persistent cold storage. T2 / T3 Hierarchical Merging : When T1 blocks approach token budget ceilings, oldest sibling blocks merge recursively into [T2] {h2} and top-level rolling [T3] digests—yielding high resolution for recent memory and compact topology for distant history . Lossless Dereferencing : Because exact entity identifiers, quantities, and block IDs remain intact, the agent can invoke decompress(block_id) whenever verbatim source inspection is required. 5.3 Breaking Physical Context Limits ( 1.65M Code Repo QA) When input repositories exceed physical context windows—such as LongBench v2 Code Repo QA Long (averaging 1.65M tokens vs. 200K–256K model limits)—naive truncation discards over 85% of the codebase. Chunking the repository into 200K segments, compiling each into BT-L3 , and concatenating the dense outputs yields dramatic accuracy gains over truncation: Target Reader Model (Window Limit) Original Truncated Accuracy BabelTele Chunk-Compiled Accuracy Net Gain Qwen3.6 Max ( 256K ) 55.17% 62.07% +6.90% GLM-5.1 ( 200K ) 62.07% 72.41% +10.34% Kimi 2.5 / 2.6 ( 256K ) 44.82% 48.28% +3.46% Next Chapter : Chapter 06 — Cross-Model Consensus & Three-Tier Safety Audit Gateway →

title: 06 · Cross-Model & Audit Gateway
desc: Portability across 19 proprietary and open-weight LLMs, dense vs. sparse MoE scaling, and Tier 1–3 deterministic anchor verification, semantic guardrails, and human Sidecar Decoders.
body: Chapter 06 — Cross-Model Consensus & Three-Tier Safety Audit Gateway ← Chapter 05: Agentic Protocol Stack & SMFT · Back to Portal (README_EN) · Next: Chapter 07 — Canonical Instruction Set → 6.1 Is BabelTele a Universal Cipher? Cross-Model Portability Laws If compressed strings could only be read by the exact model that generated them, BabelTele would be merely a brittle private shorthand. Cross-model transfer evaluations across 19 proprietary and open-weight models on LongBench v2-Short (180 samples) and QuALITY (214 QA items) establish two asymmetric laws of cross-model consensus : Law I: Compressor Aggressiveness Shapes Reader Portability Ultra-Aggressive Compressors (e.g., Gemini 3.1 Pro, >95% default compression) : Retain high self-reading fidelity but impose steeper reasoning demands on smaller heterogeneous readers. Balanced High-Portability Compressors (e.g., GPT-5.4 at ~75% , Claude Sonnet 4.6 at ~80–85% ) : Produce symbolic graphs with the broadest zero-shot portability across open and closed model families. Architectural Rule : In heterogeneous multi-agent clusters, assign models with balanced multilingual-symbolic alignment (or lock BT-L2 explicitly) as upstream compilers so downstream lightweight models can decode effortlessly. Law II: Active Capacity Over Raw Parameter Count Fixing an aggressive Gemini 3.1 Pro upstream compressor and varying Qwen-family readers on QuALITY reveals non-monotonic scale sensitivity: Downstream Reader Model Uncompressed Accuracy BabelTele Accuracy Drop (pct) Relative Retention Qwen3-14B 78.97% 64.02% -14.95 81.07% Qwen3.5-27B (Dense) 91.59% 80.84% -10.75 88.26% Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (MoE) 90.65% 75.70% -14.95 83.51% Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (MoE) 93.93% 79.91% -14.02 85.07% Qwen3.6-Max-Preview 90.19% 79.44% -10.75 88.08% Notably, dense Qwen3.5-27B ( 88.26% retention) outperforms sparse MoE Qwen3.5-397B-A17B ( 85.07% ), indicating that active parameter density and symbolic post-training quality govern decoding resilience more strongly than total parameter count alone. 6.2 Confronting Opacity: Numeric Drift & Alignment Risks Replacing human-readable prose with dense symbolic strings introduces two legitimate engineering concerns: Silent Numeric or Boundary Drift : Subtle operator flips (e.g., <= 20 vs. < 20 ) in legal, medical, or financial payloads are hard for human operators to spot by naked eye. Audit Opacity : Keyword-regex firewalls (legacy WAFs) and casual human log skimming lose visibility if inter-agent payloads are opaque. 6.3 The Three-Tier Deterministic Fidelity & Safety Audit Gateway Analogous to Bitcoin's Simplified Payment Verification (SPV) and deterministic script validation, BT-Spec v1.0 pairs model-native compression with a mandatory Three-Tier Audit Gateway : flowchart LR Src["Source Text x"] --> Comp["BabelTele Compiler C"] Comp --> BT["Candidate Payload z"] subgraph Gateway["Three-Tier Audit Gateway (BT-Audit)"] T1["Tier-1 Literal Anchor Check (<2ms): Regex extraction & bit-exact match of all numbers/units/IDs"] T2["Tier-2 Cross-Model Blind Consensus & Semantic Guardrail: Independent verifier + injection scan"] T3["Tier-3 Human Sidecar Decoder: On-demand lossless rendering in observability dashboards"] end BT --> T1 --> T2 --> Verified["Signed Verified BT Payload"] BT -. "Hover / Alert Inspection" .-> T3 Tier-1 Deterministic Literal Anchor Check ( < 2ms , Zero LLM Cost) Pure standard-library code mechanically extracts an Anchor Lexicon from source $x$ —every number, percentage, scientific exponent, version tag, code identifier, and BIBREF token—and verifies bit-exact presence in $z$ . Any unapproved rounding or omission triggers immediate rejection. Tier-2 Cross-Model Blind Verification & Semantic Guardrails Knowledge Commits : High-stakes corpus entries are audited blindly (without source access) against deterministic contract assertions by an independent model family. Semantic Guardrails : Because safety-classifier LLMs also read BabelTele zero-shot, upgrading gateway firewalls from brittle keyword regexes to lightweight semantic guardrail models enables real-time prompt-injection and policy enforcement directly over compressed traffic. Tier-3 Human-in-the-Loop Sidecar Decoder Just as CPUs execute binary machine code while debuggers disassemble it on demand, observability dashboards attach a read-only Sidecar Decoder —incurring zero runtime overhead during normal machine execution while rendering crystal-clear natural language whenever a human engineer inspects a trace. body: Chapter 07 — The Canonical BabelTele Compiler & Decoder Instruction Set ← Chapter 06: Cross-Model Consensus & Audit Gateway · Back to Portal (README_EN) · Next: Chapter 08 — Genealogy, Errata & Ecosystem → This chapter provides the five production-ready Canonical Compiler & Decoder System Prompts standardized from arXiv:2606.19857 (Appendix C) and open-source engineering ( BabelTeleSkill ), followed by the complete index of all 14 empirical prompt probes ( C.1 and BT-P1 – BT-P13 ). Append source content directly after the chosen instruction block. 7.1 Compiler Selection Decision Tree flowchart TD In["Source Input x"] --> Q{"Primary Workload?"} Q -- "General Long Docs / Meetings / Cross-Model QA" --> C1["BT-Core Standard Compiler (C.1 / BT-P7)"] Q -- "Agent Episodic Memory / Multi-Entity Causal Chains" --> C2["BT-Memory Checklist Compiler (BT-P1)"] Q -- "Code Repositories / APIs / Legal & RFC Specs" --> C3["BT-Skeleton Pure ASCII Compiler (BT-P8 / P13)"] Q -- "Extreme Token Budget / Flat Key-Value Configs" --> C4["BT-Zero Overhead Compiler (BT-P2)"] Q -- "Human UX Delivery / Tier-3 Compliance Audit" --> Dec["BT-Decoder Lossless Restorer"] 7.2 BT-Core : Standard General-Purpose Compiler ( C.1 / BT-P7 ) Recommended Tier : BT-L2 (~65%–72% token reduction, peak cross-model compatibility) Copy Your task: compress verbose human text into a minimal token sequence. The audience is not human, but another equally intelligent LLM. Core Directive: 1. Omnilingual: Ignore single-language grammar; traverse all human languages (Chinese, English, German compounds, Japanese kanji, Latin roots, etc.) and pick the highest information-density words for the target tokenizer. 2. Symbolic Collapse: Replace conjunctions, prepositions, emotions, and verbose clauses with compact mathematical/logical operators (=>, ->, &, |, !, ∈, !=) and high-frequency symbols. 3. Universality: Any LLM must fully understand the compressed output zero-shot without an external codebook. 4. Lossless: Retain all core semantics, entity bindings, exact quantities, units, and details verbatim without rounding or hallucination. Directly output the compressed text without any preface. Compress the content below: 7.3 BT-Memory : Adaptive Latent-Checklist Compiler ( BT-P1 ) Recommended Tier : BT-L1 – BT-L2 (SMFT T1/T2 episodic memory folding & complex relational graphs) Copy # Role: LLM-Native Semantic Compressor You are compiling long text into an "LLM-native high-density communication representation" with the shortest possible token sequence. [Highest Directive]: The recipient is an equally intelligent LLM. Completely discard human readability, prose grammar, and verbose JSON/bracket wrappers. # Level 1: Syntactic Freedom — Maximize Token Density 1. Omnilingual: Move freely across human languages (English, Chinese, German compounds, Japanese kanji, Latin roots) to select lexical units with maximal single-token semantic density. 2. Symbolic Collapse: Use compact logical operators (∀, ∃, ∈, =>, ->, &, !) and punctuation to replace prepositions, conjunctions, and explanatory clauses. 3. Adaptive Routing: Forbid verbose fixed labels like `Meta:` or `Entity:`. Use single-character anchors dynamically. # Level 2: Semantic Attention Checklist — Guarantee Exact Fidelity Maintain strict attention to preserve the following five dimensions losslessly: 1. Entities & Graphs: Bind people, organizations, and concepts accurately to their attributes without confusing ownership or dependency direction. 2. Exact Quantities: Preserve all numbers, metrics, units, formulas, and hyperparameters verbatim. Estimation or rounding is strictly forbidden. 3. Logic & Boundaries: Clearly retain conditional branches (?cond => act), causal chains, and exceptions (!target:detail). 4. Comparisons: Preserve multi-target comparison matrices and experimental conclusions accurately. 5. Anti-Hallucination: Preserve original placeholders (e.g., `BIBREF`, `TABREF`) character-for-character. Never invent missing facts; mark unknowns with `?` or `NULL`. Directly output the compressed "Babel-Telegraph" without any preface: 7.4 BT-Skeleton : Pure ASCII Code & Specification Compiler ( BT-P13 ) Recommended Tier : BT-L2 – BT-L3-ASCII (1.65M+ code repositories, API schemas, legal contracts — zero multi-byte Emoji inflation) Copy # Role: LLM-Native Structural Skeleton Compressor Task: Compress the input into an ultra-dense "Babel-Telegraph" for another LLM. Abandon human prose readability and select the fewest-token vocabulary across languages. # Mandatory Single-Character ASCII Anchors (Verbose English labels are forbidden) Use the following pure ASCII skeleton to maximize code-parsing attention and prevent multi-byte BPE splits: 1. Module & Macros: Use `#topic` for macro sections. Define recurring long terms on first use via `@[abbr=full_name]`. 2. Entities & Attributes: Bind attributes via `@entity(K:V)`. Flatten parallel items as `[A,B,C]`. 3. Exact Parameters: Never round or drop numbers; encode as `$param:V(unit)`. 4. Logic & Flow: Use `A->B->C` for pipelines/causality; `?[condition]=>[action]` for branches; `!object:detail` for exceptions/limits. 5. Comparisons: Use `A<>B:conclusion` for comparative evaluations. 6. Unknowns & Placeholders: Keep identifiers and `BIBREF` verbatim. Mark unspecified or ambiguous values strictly as `NULL` or `?`. Directly output the compressed result with no commentary: 7.5 BT-Zero : Zero-Overhead Flat Key-Value Compiler ( BT-P2 ) Recommended Tier : BT-L3 (Extreme context budgets & dense configuration/metric tables) Copy # Role: Extreme Zero-Overhead Semantic Compressor Compress the text below into the shortest possible token sequence for a top-tier LLM. Abandon all human reading conventions and extra line breaks. 1. Babel Traversal: Cross English, Chinese, Japanese kanji, and German compounds to pick minimal-token words. 2. Symbolic Collapse: Forbid long labels (`Meta`, `Entity`, `Condition`); map relations via `->`, `<->`, `=>`, `&`, `|`, `!`, `∈`. 3. Zero Wrapper Overhead: Extract flat `K=V` pairs separated by single characters (`|`, `^`, `~`) without token-heavy JSON braces or quotes. Keep all formulas, exact numbers, and hyperparameters 100% verbatim. 4. Anti-Hallucination Lock: Retain conditional boundaries, comparative matrices, and `BIBREF` verbatim; mark unknowns as `?` or `NULL`. Output only the compressed string: 7.6 BT-Decoder : Lossless Human-Audit Restorer Use Case : Tier-3 human observability dashboards, compliance review, and final user-facing rendering Copy # Role: BabelTele Lossless Decoder Task: Reconstruct the provided high-density BabelTele intermediate representation into clear, fluent, professional natural language (English, or the user's requested target language). Strict Decoding Rules: 1. Complete Structural Expansion: Unpack all cross-lingual tokens, logical operators (`=>`, `?=>`, `!:`, `<>`), inline macro definitions, and entity-attribute bindings without omitting any branch or caveat. 2. Exact Numeric Conservation: Every number, unit, formula, version string, code identifier, and placeholder must match the encoded input character-for-character. 3. Zero Hallucination: Never extrapolate external facts not present in the payload; explicitly state "unspecified in source" wherever `NULL`, `?`, or `@Uncertain` appears. body: Chapter 08 — Academic Genealogy, Empirical Errata & Open-Source Ecosystem ← Chapter 07: Canonical Instruction Set · Back to Portal (README_EN) · Read Single-File Whitepaper (WHITEPAPER_EN) 8.1 Comparative Taxonomy of Context Compression & M2M Paradigms Dimension Extractive / Abstractive Prose (Selective Context, LLMLingua-2, RECOMP) Continuous Latent Vectors (Gist Tokens, AutoCompressors, Activation Beacon, Interlat) Constrained Telegraphese / Fixed Metalanguages (1866 Telegraphese, Caveman, MetaGlyph) The BabelTele System (BT-Spec v1.0 / arXiv:2606.19857) Physical Carrier Discrete natural-language prose Continuous hidden-state tensors / KV-cache soft vectors Monolingual abridged text or hand-crafted symbol tables Discrete omnilingual & formal-logic symbolic graphs Human Legibility High – Medium Zero (opaque float arrays) Medium (human-skimmable) Low (opaque by default; lossless on-demand decoding) Black-Box API Support ✅ Native ❌ No (requires weight access & custom architectures) ✅ Native ✅ Native (zero-shot prompt compilation, no fine-tuning) Cross-Family Portability ✅ Supported ❌ Incompatible across heterogeneous hidden dimensions ✅ Supported ✅ Zero-shot cross-family comprehension Deep Compression Fidelity (<30% Retention) Low (token deletion breaks negation/syntax; summaries drop facts) High (within homogeneous fine-tuned model) Moderate (bounded by single-language word length) Very High (up to 99.5% QA fidelity at 27.9% length) Deterministic Auditability Naked-eye reading Unauditable black-box vectors Naked-eye reading 3-Tier mechanical anchor check + Sidecar Decoder 8.2 Official Errata on Viral Misconceptions Erratum 1: The Photosynthesis Micro-Example & Subword Token Counting Viral Corrupted String : 光合: CO2+H2O::(ox/red)<>O2!+Glucose.💧-e-,CO2+e- (secondary blogs misread poor screenshot OCR, falsely claiming <> meant "reversible" and ! meant "emphasis"). Verified Primary Figure ( arXiv:2606.19857 §3.2) : ```text 🌿光合: CO2+H2O ⇨(ox/red)⇨ O2↑ + Glucose. 💧-e⁻, CO2+e⁻. ``` Verification Notes : The original figure begins with 🌿 ( plants ), uses unidirectional hollow arrows ⇨ ... ⇨ (forward transformation), and standard chemistry gas-evolution notation O2↑ . While the paper's schematic figure labels the compression as 45 tokens -> 11 tokens (reflecting whitespace-delimited visual chunks), strict BPE subword tokenization ( tiktoken cl100k_base / o200k_base ) encodes the viral string into 33 / 32 tokens due to multi-byte punctuation/emoji splits. Under BT-Spec v1.0 ASCII rules ( Photosynthesis(plants): CO2+H2O ->(ox/red)-> O2^ + Glucose; H2O -e-, CO2 +e-. ), true BPE count drops cleanly to 19 tokens. Erratum 2: Complete Five-University Authorship & Fidelity Definition Large Language Models Do Not Always Need Readable Language ( arXiv:2606.19857 ) was authored jointly across five institutions : Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Jiayi Zhu, Linfeng Zhang), The University of Sydney (Haoxuan Peng), Hefei University of Technology (Junxi Wang), Xi'an Jiaotong University (Liang Ke), and Nanjing University (Chen Zhang). The headline metric ( 99.5% semantic fidelity at 27.9% length) measures normalized downstream QA accuracy retention relative to uncompressed inputs—not verbatim character-for-character reconstruction of original prose style. Erratum 3: BabelTele vs. GibberLink & The RL Roadmap Distinction from GibberLink : Unlike PennyroyalTea/gibberlink —where voice agents switch from spoken English to ggwave audio-modem frequencies—BabelTele operates purely within discrete text tokens by relaxing human readability priors. End-to-End RL Trajectory : As first author Jiayi Zhu noted in his June 2026 Shangguan News interview, current BabelTele relies on prompt-elicited generation; the next research frontier trains native RL compressors optimizing joint BPE length and cross-model QA recovery directly. 8.3 Global Open-Source Ecosystem & Public Datasets A. Open-Source Libraries & Tooling 1cyberlangke1/BabelTeleSkill — Modular Agent Skill packaging all 14 canonical prompt probes ( C.1 , BT-P1 – BT-P13 ) across four engineering scenarios (MIT). 1cyberlangke1/compressed-context — OpenCode context-compression plugin (npm) implementing T1 -> T2 -> T3 hierarchical memory folding with lossless rollback. AliFlux/langchain-babeltele — Python/PyPI package ( pip install langchain-babeltele ) providing LangChain document compressors, history middleware, fidelity checks, and fallbacks. lukaszgryglicki/babeltele — Offline, token-aware Rust UNIX filter supporting 19 languages, JSON, code, CSV, and logs with dual -O tokens vs. -O chars optimization targets. mikenrafter/babeltele — CLI & NixOS module delivering automated compaction hooks for Claude Code ( PreCompact ), Codex ( SessionStart compact), and Cursor ( preCompact ). m-rui001/babeltele — 95 multi-source primary specification entries reconciled in BabelTele with a zero-dependency 3-tier mechanical audit suite ( audit.py ). B. Hugging Face Empirical Datasets m-rui/babeltele-squad-encodings — SQuAD passages encoded in BabelTele ( 30.56% char retention; 90.38% fidelity on unmemorized context-dependent QA). m-rui/babeltele-chinese-encodings — 240 Chinese passages paired with 942 factual probes and iterative verification logs ( 33.0% char retention). m-rui/babeltele-coig-cqia-compressed — Compressed Chinese QA records ( 32.1% char / 29.2% token retention). 8.4 Seven-Step Production Evaluation Protocol Before deploying BabelTele in production pipelines, teams should execute this seven-step benchmark protocol: Lock Versions & Tokenizers : Pin exact upstream compiler version, downstream reader version, target BPE tokenizer, and temperature. Use Unmemorized Corpus : Test on private or post-cutoff documents containing names, exact numbers, negations, and nested exceptions; run a no-context baseline to rule out parametric memorization. Match Token Budgets : Compare uncompressed prose, standard summaries, structured bullet lists, LLMLingua-2, and BabelTele at identical real BPE budgets. Enforce Task-Agnostic Compilation : Never expose downstream test questions to the compressor; evaluate factual QA, relational reasoning, and honest abstention ( ? / NULL ). Full-Lifecycle Cost Accounting : Log characters, true BPE input tokens, compiler input/output cost, reader CoT tokens, wall-clock latency, and total API spend. Multi-Hop Drift Testing : Measure cumulative semantic drift across multi-agent relays and T1 -> T2 -> T3 memory merges. Archive Audit Trails : Retain cold-storage originals and Tier-1 literal anchor logs; fluent decoding prose alone is never proof of factual accuracy.
